reader.requirement: At --std 85 the KEY IS data-name-1 operand of a Format-2 READ on an indexed file must be refused unless it names the file's RECORD KEY or an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY data item (qualified or not), or the item at the identical character positions in another record description entry of that file (§1985:IX.2.7.4 GR3 / IX.2.5.4 GR4 implicit keys; every key is category alphanumeric per IX.2.7.3 SR2).

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the post-1985 SOURCE-form record key (construct record-key-source-2002, COBOL0900) so READ's record-key-name-1 arm is unreachable at 85

reader.edition-search: grep of KeyedIoBinder.cs for Edition/Version: ctx.Edition appears only as the diagnostic sink; RecordLayout.KeyIndexOfKeyItem and KeyIndexAtOffset consult no edition. The SR check itself is one arm for every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the data-name-1 identity/implicit-key screen is one arm; only the 2002+ record-key-name-1 (SOURCE key) form is refused at 85, which 1985 has no syntax for
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses exercise refmod, numeric twin and own-record REDEFINES refusals; not the accept half (prime/alternate/qualified/implicit twin read at run time), a key of another file, a WORKING-STORAGE item, a subordinate prefix of the key, or a shorter same-position item

probes.expected: all accepted; reads by the named key (SR2, IX.2.7.4 GR3, IX.2.5.4 GR4)

reader.notes: One identity-or-implicit-key screen serves every edition and matches the 1985 text, whose RECORD KEY GR3 and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY GR4 give the same implicit keys the 2023 code comments cite. The COBOL0864 message cites §2023:14.9.30.3 SR11 even at --std 85 (cosmetic: the refusal is right).

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-240/src/r1-sub-run.cob (FD IXF RECORD KEY IX-KEY PIC X(4); second 01 IX-REC2 with 05 IX-T PIC X(4) OCCURS 2): READ IXF KEY IS IX-T (1) compiles and runs at --std 85, printing 'R1 TWO' (runs/r1-sub-run-001); the same at --std 2023 (runs/r1-sub-run-002). The 1985 format prints KEY IS data-name-1 and SR3 lets it be qualified only; a table element must be subscripted (IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR4, no READ KEY exception), so an item under OCCURS has no legal reading as data-name-1 and is never 'a data item specified as a record key'. Same reading the tree took for PADDING CHARACTER in kb/Work PB5499. KeyedIoBinder.BindRead reads the operand through ResolveSending + KeyIndexOfKeyItem(keyOccurrence) and never calls DataBinder.ScreenDataNameShape (COBOL2024), which it does call for the record-key-name arm (RecordKeyNameOf). Other probes upheld the reader: group twin and file-name qualification IX-KEY OF IXF accepted and read right (r1-grp-twin: R1 TWO, R2 ONE); alphanumeric-edited twin refused COBOL0864 (r1-edit-twin); condition-name refused COBOL1639 (r1-cond). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR2  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR3  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR4  (4.3.8.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4'; 'OK  §1985:IX.2.7.4 GR3  (2.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3'.
